claim: The FLT3 Internal Tandem Duplication (FLT3ITD) mutation is common in adult acute myeloid leukemia (AML).
source: The FLT3 Internal Tandem Duplication (FLT3ITD) mutation is common in adult acute myeloid leukemia (AML) but rare in early childhood AML.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as established context for the study.

claim: The FLT3ITD mutation is rare in early childhood AML.
source: The FLT3 Internal Tandem Duplication (FLT3ITD) mutation is common in adult acute myeloid leukemia (AML) but rare in early childhood AML.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as established context for the study.

claim: Flt3ITD mutations cause hematopoietic stem cell depletion during adult but not fetal stages of murine development.
source: Here we show that Flt3ITD and cooperating Flt3ITD/Runx1 mutations cause hematopoietic stem cell depletion and myeloid progenitor expansion during adult but not fetal stages of murine development.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data in Figures 1-3.

claim: Flt3ITD mutations cause myeloid progenitor expansion during adult but not fetal stages of murine development.
source: Here we show that Flt3ITD and cooperating Flt3ITD/Runx1 mutations cause hematopoietic stem cell depletion and myeloid progenitor expansion during adult but not fetal stages of murine development.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data in Figures 1-3.

claim: Cooperating Flt3ITD/Runx1 mutations cause hematopoietic stem cell depletion during adult but not fetal stages of murine development.
source: Here we show that Flt3ITD and cooperating Flt3ITD/Runx1 mutations cause hematopoietic stem cell depletion and myeloid progenitor expansion during adult but not fetal stages of murine development.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data in Figure 3.

claim: FLT3ITD induces self-renewal programs via STAT5-dependent mechanisms in adult progenitors.
source: In adult progenitors, FLT3ITD simultaneously induces self-renewal and myeloid commitment programs via STAT5-dependent and STAT5-independent mechanisms, respectively.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data in Figures 6 and 7.

claim: FLT3ITD induces myeloid commitment programs via STAT5-independent mechanisms in adult progenitors.
source: In adult progenitors, FLT3ITD simultaneously induces self-renewal and myeloid commitment programs via STAT5-dependent and STAT5-independent mechanisms, respectively.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data in Figures 6 and 7.

claim: FLT3ITD can activate STAT5 signal transduction prior to birth.
source: While FLT3ITD can activate STAT5 signal transduction prior to birth, this signaling does not alter gene expression until hematopoietic progenitors transition from fetal to adult transcriptional states.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by Western blot data in Figure 4.

claim: FLT3ITD signaling does not alter gene expression until hematopoietic progenitors transition from fetal to adult transcriptional states.
source: While FLT3ITD can activate STAT5 signal transduction prior to birth, this signaling does not alter gene expression until hematopoietic progenitors transition from fetal to adult transcriptional states.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by gene expression data in Figures 7 and 8.

claim: Cooperative interactions between Flt3ITD and Runx1 mutations are blunted in fetal/neonatal progenitors.
source: Cooperative interactions between Flt3ITD and Runx1 mutations are also blunted in fetal/neonatal progenitors.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data in Figures 3 and 9.

claim: Fetal/neonatal progenitors are protected from leukemic transformation because they are not competent to express FLT3ITD target genes.
source: Fetal/neonatal progenitors may therefore be protected from leukemic transformation because they are not competent to express FLT3ITD target genes.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the abstract based on the experimental findings.

claim: Changes in the transcriptional states of developing hematopoietic progenitors may shape the mutation spectra of human leukemias.
source: Changes in the transcriptional states of developing hematopoietic progenitors may generally shape the mutation spectra of human leukemias.
evidence: This is a speculative conclusion stated in the abstract based on the experimental findings.

claim: Flt3 is more highly expressed in HPCs than in HSCs at both fetal and adult ages.
source: Flt3 was more highly expressed in HPCs than in HSCs at both ages (Figure 1A), consistent with prior studies (Buza-Vidas et al., 2011)
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 1A and a citation to prior literature.

claim: Flt3 expression does not change with age in HSCs.
source: but its expression did not change with age in either cell population (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Flt3 expression does not change with age in HPCs.
source: but its expression did not change with age in either cell population (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: The FLT3 protein is expressed in both fetal and adult progenitors.
source: Flow cytometry confirmed that the FLT3 protein is expressed in both fetal and adult progenitors (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Adult Flt3ITD/+ mice have approximately 50% fewer HSCs than wild type littermates.
source: Adult Flt3ITD/+ mice had ~50% fewer HSCs than wild type littermates, consistent with prior studies, and Flt3ITD/ITD mice had a near-complete loss of phenotypic HSCs (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is supported by HSC quantification data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Adult Flt3ITD/ITD mice have a near-complete loss of phenotypic HSCs.
source: Adult Flt3ITD/+ mice had ~50% fewer HSCs than wild type littermates, consistent with prior studies, and Flt3ITD/ITD mice had a near-complete loss of phenotypic HSCs (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is supported by HSC quantification data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: HSC depletion in the bone marrow of Flt3ITD mice is not accompanied by extramedullary expansion of HSCs in the spleen.
source: HSC depletion in the bone marrow was not accompanied by extramedullary expansion of HSCs in the spleen (Figure 1E), in contrast to other leukemogenic mutations (e.g. Pten deletion) that cause depletion of bone marrow HSCs but marked expansion of the spleen HSC population (Magee et al., 2012; Porter et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by HSC frequency data shown in Figure 1E and contrasted with cited literature.

claim: Flt3ITD/+ and Flt3ITD/ITD fetal mice have similar numbers of HSCs as wild type littermates.
source: Unlike adult mice, Flt3ITD/+ and Flt3ITD/ITD fetal mice had similar numbers of HSCs as wild type littermates (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is supported by HSC quantification data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Adult Flt3ITD/ITD bone marrow has significantly fewer functional HSCs than adult wild type bone marrow.
source: Adult Flt3ITD/ITD bone marrow had significantly fewer functional HSCs than adult wild type bone marrow (p<0.00001, Figure 1F).
evidence: This is supported by limiting dilution transplantation data shown in Figure 1F.

claim: Wild type and Flt3ITD/ITD fetal livers have similar HSC frequencies.
source: In contrast, wild type and Flt3ITD/ITD fetal livers had similar HSC frequencies (Figure 1G).
evidence: This is supported by limiting dilution transplantation data shown in Figure 1G.

claim: Donor Flt3ITD/ITD HSCs are significantly depleted in primary recipients of fetal liver cells.
source: Donor Flt3ITD/ITD HSCs were significantly depleted in primary recipient mice, but wild type competitor HSCs were not (Figure 1H).
evidence: This is supported by donor HSC chimerism data shown in Figure 1H.

claim: Overall donor bone marrow chimerism is not significantly different between recipients of wild type and Flt3ITD/ITD fetal liver cells.
source: Overall donor bone marrow chimerism was not significantly different between recipients of wild type and Flt3ITD/ITD fetal liver cells (Figure 1I).
evidence: This is supported by donor bone marrow chimerism data shown in Figure 1I.

claim: Fetal Flt3ITD/ITD HSCs are functional.
source: Thus, fetal Flt3ITD/ITD HSCs are functional, but they lose repopulating activity after transplantation into adult recipient mice.
evidence: This is inferred from the transplantation data showing initial engraftment but subsequent depletion.

claim: Fetal Flt3ITD/ITD HSCs lose repopulating activity after transplantation into adult recipient mice.
source: Thus, fetal Flt3ITD/ITD HSCs are functional, but they lose repopulating activity after transplantation into adult recipient mice.
evidence: This is supported by secondary transplantation data shown in Figures 1J and 1K.

claim: Flt3ITD/+ and Flt3ITD/ITD mice have normal HSC numbers at all ages prior to birth.

claim: HSC depletion is evident at P14 in both the bone marrow and the spleen of Flt3ITD mice.
source: HSC depletion was evident at P14 in both the bone marrow and the spleen, though not to the extent observed in adult bone marrow (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is supported by HSC quantification data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: A modest increase in Flt3ITD/+ and Flt3ITD/ITD HPCs and GMPs is observed at P0.
source: We observed a modest increase in Flt3ITD/+and Flt3ITD/ITD HPCs and GMPs at P0 (Figure 2C,E)
evidence: This is supported by HPC and GMP quantification data shown in Figures 2C and 2E.

claim: HPC and GMP expansion becomes more severe by P14 in Flt3ITD/ITD mice.
source: and this phenotype became more severe, particularly in Flt3ITD/ITD mice, by P14 (Figure 2D,E).
evidence: This is supported by HPC and GMP quantification data shown in Figures 2D and 2E.

claim: Spleen enlargement due to MPN is evident by P14 in Flt3ITD/+ and Flt3ITD/ITD mice.
source: Spleen enlargement due to MPN was evident by P14 in Flt3ITD/+and Flt3ITD/ITD mice, but E14.5, E16.5 and P0 liver sizes were not increased relative to wild type littermates (Figure 2F).
evidence: This is supported by spleen and liver weight data shown in Figure 2F.

claim: E14.5, E16.5 and P0 liver sizes are not increased in Flt3ITD mice relative to wild type littermates.

claim: Only 1 of 15 recipients of Flt3ITD/+; Runx1Δ/+ P21 donor cells had multi-lineage donor chimerism.

claim: All recipients of control and Flt3ITD/+; Runx1Δ/+ P0 donor cells had multi-lineage donor chimerism.

claim: Sustained MAPK pathway signaling is not required for HSC depletion, HPC expansion and GMP expansion in Flt3ITD/+ adult mice.
source: This suggests that sustained MAPK pathway signaling is not required for HSC depletion, HPC expansion and GMP expansion in Flt3ITD/+ adult mice.
evidence: This is inferred from the lack of effect of MEK inhibition on these phenotypes.

claim: PD0325901 treatment beginning at P1 does not prevent HSC depletion or HPC expansion in Flt3ITD mutant neonates.
source: it did not prevent HSC depletion or HPC expansion in Flt3ITD mutant neonates (Figure 5D,E)
evidence: This is supported by HSC and HPC quantification data shown in Figures 5D and 5E.

claim: PD0325901 treatment beginning at P1 only partially rescues GMP expansion in Flt3ITD mutant neonates.
source: and it only partially rescued GMP expansion (Figure 5F).
evidence: This is supported by GMP frequency data shown in Figure 5F.

claim: Stat5a/b deletion exacerbates the HSC depletion phenotype of Flt3ITD/+ mice.
source: Surprisingly, Stat5a/b deletion exacerbated the HSC depletion, HPC expansion and GMP expansion phenotypes of Flt3ITD/+mice rather than rescuing them (Figure 6A–C).
evidence: This is supported by HSC quantification data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: Stat5a/b deletion exacerbates the HPC expansion phenotype of Flt3ITD/+ mice.
source: Surprisingly, Stat5a/b deletion exacerbated the HSC depletion, HPC expansion and GMP expansion phenotypes of Flt3ITD/+mice rather than rescuing them (Figure 6A–C).
evidence: This is supported by HPC quantification data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: Stat5a/b deletion exacerbates the GMP expansion phenotype of Flt3ITD/+ mice.
source: Surprisingly, Stat5a/b deletion exacerbated the HSC depletion, HPC expansion and GMP expansion phenotypes of Flt3ITD/+mice rather than rescuing them (Figure 6A–C).
evidence: This is supported by GMP frequency data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: Spleen weights are enlarged in Flt3ITD; Stat5Δ/+ and Flt3ITD/+; Stat5Δ/Δ mice relative to control, Stat5Δ/+, Stat5Δ/Δ and Flt3ITD/+ littermates.
source: Spleen weights were also enlarged in Flt3ITD; Stat5Δ/+ and Flt3ITD/+; Stat5Δ/Δ mice relative to control, Stat5Δ/+, Stat5Δ/Δ and Flt3ITD/+ littermates (Figure 5D).
evidence: This is supported by spleen weight data shown in Figure 6D.

claim: Flt3ITD/+; Stat5a/bf/+; Vav1-Cre mice have fewer HSCs than control or Flt3ITD/+ littermates at 8-10 weeks after birth.
source: Nevertheless, Flt3ITD/+; Stat5a/bf/+; Vav1-Cre mice had fewer HSCs, more HPCs, more GMPs and larger spleens than control or Flt3ITD/+ littermates at 8–10 weeks after birth (Figure 6E–H).
evidence: This is supported by HSC quantification data shown in Figure 6E.

claim: Flt3ITD/+; Stat5a/bf/+; Vav1-Cre mice have more HPCs than control or Flt3ITD/+ littermates at 8-10 weeks after birth.
source: Nevertheless, Flt3ITD/+; Stat5a/bf/+; Vav1-Cre mice had fewer HSCs, more HPCs, more GMPs and larger spleens than control or Flt3ITD/+ littermates at 8–10 weeks after birth (Figure 6E–H).
evidence: This is supported by HPC quantification data shown in Figure 6F.

claim: Flt3ITD/+; Stat5a/bf/+; Vav1-Cre mice have more GMPs than control or Flt3ITD/+ littermates at 8-10 weeks after birth.
source: Nevertheless, Flt3ITD/+; Stat5a/bf/+; Vav1-Cre mice had fewer HSCs, more HPCs, more GMPs and larger spleens than control or Flt3ITD/+ littermates at 8–10 weeks after birth (Figure 6E–H).
evidence: This is supported by GMP frequency data shown in Figure 6G.

claim: Flt3ITD/+; Stat5a/bf/+; Vav1-Cre mice have larger spleens than control or Flt3ITD/+ littermates at 8-10 weeks after birth.
source: Nevertheless, Flt3ITD/+; Stat5a/bf/+; Vav1-Cre mice had fewer HSCs, more HPCs, more GMPs and larger spleens than control or Flt3ITD/+ littermates at 8–10 weeks after birth (Figure 6E–H).
evidence: This is supported by spleen weight data shown in Figure 6H.

claim: 254 annotated coding genes are differentially expressed between wild type and Flt3ITD/+ HPCs at one or more time points.
source: In experiment 1, we identified 254 annotated coding genes that were differentially expressed between wild type and Flt3ITD/+ HPCs at one or more time points (Figure 7—source data 1; adjusted p<0.05; fold change ≥ 2).
evidence: This is supported by microarray data analysis from experiment 1.

claim: No genes meet stringent filtering criteria for differential expression in Flt3ITD HSCs.
source: We did not identify any genes that met these stringent filtering criteria in HSCs, though statistically significant changes in gene expression were observed when specific target genes (from the HPC list) were individually interrogated (p<0.05, Figure 7—source data 1).
evidence: This is supported by microarray data analysis from experiment 1.

claim: 58 unique genes are differentially expressed between wild type and Flt3ITD/+ HPCs in both experiments 1 and 2.
source: Of the 254 genes that were differentially expressed in experiment 1, 58 unique genes were also differentially expressed between wild type and Flt3ITD/+ HPCs in experiment 2 (Figure 7B and Figure 7—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by microarray data analysis comparing experiments 1 and 2.

claim: 33 genes are expressed at higher levels in Flt3ITD HPCs relative to wild type HPCs.
source: Thirty-three genes were expressed at higher levels in Flt3ITD HPCs relative to wild type HPCs, and 25 genes were expressed at lower levels (Figure 7B).
evidence: This is supported by the heatmap shown in Figure 7B.

claim: 25 genes are expressed at lower levels in Flt3ITD HPCs relative to wild type HPCs.
source: Thirty-three genes were expressed at higher levels in Flt3ITD HPCs relative to wild type HPCs, and 25 genes were expressed at lower levels (Figure 7B).
evidence: This is supported by the heatmap shown in Figure 7B.

claim: 35 of the 58 differentially expressed genes normalize when Stat5a/b is deleted.
source: Of these, 35 normalized when Stat5a/b was deleted, but 23 did not.
evidence: This is supported by microarray data analysis comparing Flt3ITD/+ and Flt3ITD/+; Stat5Δ/Δ HPCs.

claim: 23 of the 58 differentially expressed genes do not normalize when Stat5a/b is deleted.
source: Of these, 35 normalized when Stat5a/b was deleted, but 23 did not.
evidence: This is supported by microarray data analysis comparing Flt3ITD/+ and Flt3ITD/+; Stat5Δ/Δ HPCs.

claim: FLT3ITD has both STAT5-dependent and STAT5-independent effects on gene expression.
source: FLT3ITD therefore has both STAT5-dependent and STAT5-independent effects on gene expression, and these effects are more pronounced in HPCs as compared to HSCs.
evidence: This is inferred from the microarray data showing genes that normalize or do not normalize with Stat5a/b deletion.

claim: Self-renewal-related genes are enriched in Flt3ITD/+ HPCs.
source: Self-renewal-related genes were enriched in Flt3ITD/+ HPCs, and commitment-related genes were enriched in wild type HPCs (Figure 7C).
evidence: This is supported by GSEA data shown in Figure 7C.

claim: Commitment-related genes are enriched in wild type HPCs.
source: Self-renewal-related genes were enriched in Flt3ITD/+ HPCs, and commitment-related genes were enriched in wild type HPCs (Figure 7C).
evidence: This is supported by GSEA data shown in Figure 7C.

claim: The FLT3ITD protein can activate self-renewal mechanisms in otherwise non-self-renewing HPCs.
source: This suggests that the FLT3ITD protein can activate self-renewal mechanisms in otherwise non-self-renewing HPCs.
evidence: This is inferred from the GSEA data showing enrichment of self-renewal genes in Flt3ITD/+ HPCs.

claim: Self-renewal gene enrichment in Flt3ITD/+ HPCs is strongly reversed when Stat5a/b is deleted.
source: Remarkably, these effects were strongly reversed when Stat5a/b was deleted (Figure 7C).
evidence: This is supported by GSEA data shown in Figure 7C.

claim: The most significantly enriched gene sets in Flt3ITD/+; Stat5Δ/Δ HPCs are generally associated with increased inflammatory cytokine signaling.
source: The most significantly enriched gene sets in Flt3ITD/+; Stat5Δ/Δ HPCs were generally associated with increased inflammatory cytokine signaling (Figure 7E).
evidence: This is supported by GSEA data shown in Figure 7E.

claim: Differences between wild type and Flt3ITD/+ HPCs are more evident at P14 and adulthood than at E14.5 or P0.
source: We found that differences between wild type and Flt3ITD/+ HPCs were more evident at P14 and adulthood than at E14.5 or P0 (Figure 8A and Figure 8—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by the heatmap shown in Figure 8A.

claim: Fetal, neonatal and adult hematopoietic progenitors have distinct transcriptional responses to FLT3ITD signaling.
source: Thus, fetal, neonatal and adult hematopoietic progenitors have distinct transcriptional responses to FLT3ITD signaling.
evidence: This is inferred from the temporal differences in FLT3ITD target gene expression.

claim: 2627 unique genes exhibit significant changes in gene expression in HSCs between E14.5 and adulthood.
source: We identified 2627 unique genes (from 3005 different probes) that exhibited significant changes in gene expression in HSCs between E14.5 and adulthood.
evidence: This is supported by microarray data analysis of wild type HSCs at different ages.

claim: 228 of the most differentially expressed transcripts follow a consistent trend toward increasing or decreasing expression with increasing age.
source: Of the 228 most differentially expressed transcripts (from the top 250 probes), all followed a consistent trend toward increasing (109 genes) or decreasing (119 genes) expression with increasing age, and most were differentially expressed in both HSCs and HPCs (Figure 8C, Figure 8—source data 1).
evidence: This is supported by the heatmap shown in Figure 8C and microarray data analysis.

claim: P14 HSCs more closely resemble adult HSCs than fetal HSCs.
source: Principal component analysis and Euclidean distance measurements showed that P14 HSCs more closely resembled adult HSCs than fetal HSCs, and P0 HSCs more closely resembled fetal HSCs (Figure 8E).
evidence: This is supported by principal component analysis and Euclidean distance measurements shown in Figure 8E.

claim: P0 HSCs more closely resemble fetal HSCs than adult HSCs.
source: Principal component analysis and Euclidean distance measurements showed that P14 HSCs more closely resembled adult HSCs than fetal HSCs, and P0 HSCs more closely resembled fetal HSCs (Figure 8E).
evidence: This is supported by principal component analysis and Euclidean distance measurements shown in Figure 8E.

claim: HSCs and HPCs begin transitioning from fetal to adult transcriptional programs by P14.
source: The data show that HSCs and HPCs begin transitioning from fetal to adult transcriptional programs by P14, even before they achieve quiescence (Bowie et al., 2006).
evidence: This is inferred from the principal component analysis and gene expression data, with a citation to prior literature about quiescence.

claim: HSCs and HPCs become competent to express (or repress) FLT3ITD target genes as they transition from fetal to adult transcriptional programs.
source: Furthermore, the data suggest that HSCs and HPCs become competent to express (or repress) FLT3ITD target genes as they transition from fetal to adult transcriptional programs.
evidence: This is inferred from the correlation between the timing of transcriptional transitions and FLT3ITD target gene activation.

claim: Flt3ITD and Tet2 loss of function mutations cooperatively induce changes in gene expression and DNA methylation in adult HPCs that are not observed with either mutation alone.
source: Flt3ITD and Tet2 loss of function mutations have recently been shown to cooperatively induce changes in gene expression and DNA methylation in adult HPCs that are not observed with either mutation alone (Shih et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: 191 genes are significantly differentially expressed between wild type and Flt3ITD/+; Runx1Δ/+ HPCs at P14.
source: At P14, we identified 191 genes that were significantly differentially expressed between wild type and Flt3ITD/+; Runx1Δ/+ HPCs (adj. p<0.05; fold change ≥ 3).
evidence: This is supported by microarray data analysis of P14 HPCs.

claim: Only eight genes are significantly differentially expressed between wild type and Flt3ITD/+; Runx1Δ/+ HPCs at P0.
source: At P0 only eight genes met these criteria, seven of which overlapped with the P14 gene list (Figure 9A and Figure 9—source data 1).
evidence: This is supported by microarray data analysis of P0 HPCs and the Venn diagram shown in Figure 9A.

claim: Genes differentially expressed in Flt3ITD/+; Runx1Δ/+ HPCs overlap significantly with genes differentially expressed in Flt3ITD; Tet2Δ/Δ HPCs.
source: GSEA showed significant overlap between genes that were differentially expressed in Flt3ITD/+; Runx1Δ/+ HPCs and those that Shih et al. found to be differentially expressed in Flt3ITD; Tet2Δ/Δ HPCs (Shih et al., 2015) (Figure 9B).
evidence: This is supported by GSEA data shown in Figure 9B and a citation to prior literature.

claim: FLT3ITD can cooperate with diverse mutations to induce a conserved set of target genes.
source: This suggests that FLT3ITD can cooperate with diverse mutations to induce a conserved set of target genes.
evidence: This is inferred from the overlap between genes differentially expressed in Flt3ITD/+; Runx1Δ/+ and Flt3ITD; Tet2Δ/Δ HPCs.

claim: Of the 25 most differentially expressed genes in P14 Flt3ITD/+; Runx1Δ/+ HPCs, only three are induced equally at both P0 and P14.
source: Of the 25 most differentially expressed genes in P14 Flt3ITD/+; Runx1Δ/+ HPCs, only three – Nov, Bhlhe40 and Mboat2 – were induced equally at both P0 and P14 (Figure 9D, Figure 9—source data 1).
evidence: This is supported by gene expression data shown in Figure 9D.

claim: Several Gene Ontology and Oncogenic Signature gene sets are enriched in P14 Flt3ITD/+; Runx1Δ/+ HPCs relative to wild type controls.
source: Several Gene Ontology and Oncogenic Signature gene sets were enriched in P14 Flt3ITD/+; Runx1Δ/+ HPCs relative to wild type controls, the most significant of which included genes that are negatively regulated by mTOR (Majumder et al., 2004), genes that inhibit apoptosis (Gene Ontology) and c-myc targets (Bild et al., 2006) (Figure 9E).
evidence: This is supported by GSEA data shown in Figure 9E and citations to prior literature.

claim: These gene sets are not significantly enriched in P0 HSCs with the exception of the anti-apoptotic gene set.
source: These gene sets were not significantly enriched in P0 HSCs with the exception of the anti-apoptotic gene set, which was paradoxically enriched in wild type HPCs relative to Flt3ITD/+; Runx1Δ/+ (Figure 9E).
evidence: This is supported by GSEA data shown in Figure 9E.

claim: Cooperating Flt3ITD and Runx1 mutations have developmental context-specific effects on gene expression.
source: Altogether, the data show that cooperating Flt3ITD and Runx1 mutations — and likely other cooperating mutations — have developmental context-specific effects on gene expression.
evidence: This is inferred from the differences in gene expression between P0 and P14 Flt3ITD/+; Runx1Δ/+ HPCs.
